$comment: Acceptance criteria for issue 201. Detection named an adapter that cannot read the evidence that triggered it, TWICE, while stating the rule it was breaking in a comment three lines above each call: a .beads/ SQLite store was offered adapters/execution-file (which reads .repo-governor/execution.json) and a Renovate config was offered adapters/change-signals-file (which reads a local signals file). Both were marked PROVIDER_UNCONFIRMED with an explicit not_evidence line, so nothing was concealed -- and an external reporter still read the candidate row as 'we found your beads DB, bind it', because the mitigation is a sentence and the adapter field is a machine-readable claim. WHY A NULL ADAPTER RATHER THAN A DIFFERENT LABEL: the detection is worth keeping -- the role IS present, and a user should know their beads store was seen. What cannot stand is the pointer. THE VACUITY THIS BAR IS BUILT AGAINST is pinning to .beads/. The comment in onboard.py already counts three instances of this class, so a check naming the third one passes the day a fourth appears. C1 is the general property and is checked by SPAWNING each named adapter against the repository that triggered the detection, not by grepping onboard.py -- imports.py refuses greps for this reason: a table that exists and is never read passes a source-text check. C4 and C5 name the two instances because both were shipped. CALIBRATION THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN: reachability alone is not the property. adapters/execution-file reports reachable=True on a repository that happens to carry .repo-governor/execution.json, so on one real governed repository the over-promise would have passed a naive reachability check. That is why the fixture in C1 is purpose-built and why the null adapter, not a reachability gate, is the fix.

criteria.$comment: C1 THE GENERAL PROPERTY. Every candidate that names an adapter names one reachable against the repository that triggered it. Fixture carries .beads/, renovate.json and docs/adr at once.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] every named adapter can read what its evidence cites"'

criteria.$comment: C2 FLOOR CONTROL for C1. A fixture detecting nothing makes the loop above run zero times and pass having established nothing.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -qE "\[PASS\] the over-promise fixture produced candidates \([3-9]"'

criteria.$comment: C3 A NULL ADAPTER IS NEVER SILENT. 'Found, and nothing here reads it' is useful; 'found', with no adapter and no reason, is a candidate a human cannot act on either way.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] a candidate naming no adapter says why"'

criteria.$comment: C4 INSTANCE ONE, by name, because it shipped.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] a .beads store is detected and names no adapter"'

criteria.$comment: C5 INSTANCE TWO, by name, because it shipped too and nobody had reported it.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] a renovate config is detected and names no adapter"'

criteria.$comment: C6 CONTROL -- the detection SURVIVES. Nulling the adapter must not delete the candidate; a user whose beads store went unmentioned is worse off than one told nothing reads it.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] every candidate cites evidence"'

criteria.$comment: C7 no candidate names an adapter that is not on disk.
criteria.target: bash -c 'python3 conformance/onboarding.py | grep -q "\[PASS\] every named adapter exists on disk"'
